review_blockers_addressed: P0 commit():601 finally released Database.lock unconditionally — an alias-INSERT or conn.commit() failure before the durable point left the middleware observing state=PREPARED, lock_held=False, in_txn=True (transaction open, lock gone). Fixed per design §4.5 rule 1: finally releases ONLY at/after DURABLE_COMMITTED; a PREPARED failure keeps the call lock-holding and rollback() (connection rolled back first, lock released exactly once) owns the release

P0 publish():751 exception guard covered prepare only — a commit failure escaped and left conn.in_transaction=True. Fixed with one rollback guard over prepare -> output validation -> commit (mirrors middleware.py:210 so both drivers validate output before the durable point), any failure reaches rollback() and the connection is left usable

P1 PLAN_DIGEST_MISMATCH details contradicted themselves (expected_plan_digest == recomputed_plan_digest while claiming mismatch because stored_digest stood in for the caller's input). Fixed: expected_plan_digest now reports request['plan_digest']; the stored-vs-recomputed leg already raises inside verify_digest (plan_store.py:434) with the correct pair

Case-12 coverage gaps closed in the §8 matrix: invalidated approval set refused with APPROVAL_SET_INVALIDATED + zero change (durable row-level invalidation, §4.5 staged reload reads authority_state); pre-COMMIT failure regressions x2 (forced alias INSERT raise; conn.commit is a read-only attribute so real pre-durable commit failure is forced via a connection proxy) asserting rollback-entry PREPARED+locked+in-txn, other threads locked out, single release after rollback, and the honest retry publishing
